newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, South Korea sign investment pact.
newsitem.headline: Chile, South Korea sign investment pact.

text.p: The presidents of South Korea and Chile signed an agreement to protect and promote their countries' investments on Friday, adding to Chile's growing economic links with east Asia.

Kim, who arrived on Thursday in Chile, and President Eduardo Frei held talks on trade and investment issues, including interest by South Korean businessmen in raising their stake in Chile's copper industry.

South Korea is the second-largest buyer of Chilean copper after Japan, and Koreans want to lock in a guaranteed share of copper output through investments in big mines as other countries have done, local officials said.
Frei and Kim later signed an investment promotion and protection agreement, laying the groundwork for closer economic ties, officials said.

Kim's visit came on the heels of a three-day visit to Chile by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last month. Both visits, which included large business delegations, highlighted Asia's fast-growing interest in Latin America after years of writing it off as a turbulent, unpredictable region, Chilean officials said.

In one example of growing business ties, executives from South Korea's Hyundai Corp and the National Mining Society of Chile signed on Friday an agreement to study building a giant copper smelter worth at least $300 million.

Chilean fresh fruit exporters said they received assurances from Korean officials that they had lifted all remaining restrictions on imports of Chilean fruit, opening the way for a 10-fold rise in shipments to Korea, they said.
Exporters in Chile's booming fruit industry have been moving aggressively into the Asian market after Chile announced early this year it had eradicated a minute pest: the Mediterranean fruit fly.
The fly, which spoils apples, pears, grapes and other fruit by laying its eggs in it, had kept most Chilean exports barred from nearly all of Asia, including Korea.
